purpose: Run all eight production specialists in their own GitHub runner, worktree, Aider process and local AI brain, with central evidence fan-in and operator-controlled integration.
northStar: Continuously improve Bikeztagram toward a polished, reliable creative editing product while preserving isolated specialist ownership, truthful verification and protected integration.

coordination.maxConcurrentWorkersDescription: Eight disjoint production specialist lanes: Director, Timeline, Music, Scene, Rhythm, Render, Media Intelligence and Caption.
coordination.experimentalWorkersDescription: Two disposable Aider strategy lanes used only for materialization experiments; never part of protected production activation.

activationGate.operatorControl: Controlled live activation for eight isolated production specialist workers. Each worker owns exactly one product file, runs in its own GitHub runner/worktree/Aider/local AI environment, verifies its candidate independently, and fans evidence into one central ledger. Protected integration remains operator-controlled.

owns: Aider whole-file root materialization experiment against media intelligence
Aider root-scoped diff materialization experiment against caption planning

handoffRules: Workers must write structured evidence before handing work to another worker.
A failure belongs in the failure queue when the current worker cannot safely complete or verify its task.
Repair work must be isolated from the protected builder until independently verified.
No worker may weaken a validator, safety rule, protected workflow or production gate merely to turn a failure into a pass.
Every new bot, entrypoint, path, protocol name and handoff contract must be registered here and covered by the fleet verifier before activation.
Removed or renamed bots and entrypoints must be removed from this registry and all active discovery paths at the same time.
The coordinator must never invent a worker, path or protocol that is absent from this registry.
Specialist Builders must use the shared isolated runner, explicit bot id, explicit objective and exact registry-owned file scope.
Parallel specialist work must use disjoint file scopes and isolated worktrees; overlapping scopes are a planner failure.
Specialist Builder changes must produce an explicit base/candidate commit pair for downstream Reviewer and QA handoff.
Only verified specialist handoffs may enter the central completed-work manifest as candidates.
Specialist failures must remain visible in the central completed-work manifest so the recovery layer can classify and route repairable work.
Repairable specialist product failures must preserve their exact base, declared file scope and candidate patch before recovery begins.
The specialist recovery runner may invoke the existing Repair -> QA -> Reviewer chain only for explicitly classified repairable product failures.
The recovery runner may orchestrate Repair, QA and Reviewer only after the explicit fleet activation gate is enabled.
The controlled recovery workflow must use the registered recovery runner and must never bypass the explicit enabled:true plus coordination.mode:'active' gate.
Only durations listed in activationGate.allowedTestDurations may be used for controlled live shakedowns; larger waves require a separate operator-approved activation change.
Endurance cycles must consume the previous cycle's verified cumulative branch; main remains the protected starting point and final integration remains operator-controlled.
The Evolution Engineer runs outside the production specialist lane and may observe completed-run evidence but must never become a dependency of the persistent production workflow.
Evolution experiments are opt-in, infrastructure-only, non-merging and require human review before promotion.
Evolution work may not weaken validators, production gates, specialist scopes, the persistent engine or product source.
Production specialist workers must run as six independent jobs in the dedicated specialist workflow; they must never share a production workspace or become dependencies of one another.

All six production specialist workers may execute only when the dedicated specialist workflow is explicitly dispatched; the production specialist contract remains registry-gated and protected integration remains operator-controlled.
Independent worker results must fan in through one central run ledger before any integration candidate is assembled.
A worker branch is an implementation workspace, not the source of truth; the canonical handoff is its verified base/candidate metadata plus central ledger record.
Fan-in must classify every worker as completed, review, recovery, failed or pending so no result becomes an orphaned pot.
Every production specialist must own exactly one disjoint product file; overlapping file ownership is a hard activation failure.
